dedupe_keys.name: canada combined sewer overflow volumes from wastewater systems under the wastewater systems effluent regulations

description: Environment and Climate Change Canada produced this dataset of combined sewer overflow (CSO) volumes reported by wastewater systems subject to the Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations (WSER), in force since 2012 for systems that collect an average of 100 m3 a day or more. Owners of systems with combined sewers report each year the total volume and number of days wastewater is discharged per month through CSO points because of precipitation; the map shows the annual volume from all CSO points in each system's collection area. Coverage is Canada, excluding the Northwest Territories, Nunavut and the areas of Quebec and Newfoundland and Labrador north of the 54th parallel. The data are free under the Open Government Licence - Canada as CSV and XLS, with ESRI REST and WMS services. Caveats: the volumes are mostly estimates, 999999999 marks a missing value, and no Quebec volumes are available from 2018 because an equivalency agreement applies. Simulation uses: overflow volumes by system for sewer capacity, wet-weather and climate adaptation studies. Related records: the US EPA overflow events (data-epa-echo-npdes-sewer-overflow-bypass-events) and England's storm overflow returns (data-ea-edm-storm-overflows-annual-returns).
